hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: APOE4 acidic organelles were significantly more alkaline than APOE3 organelles by 0.14 pH units, although both remained within the reported standard lysosomal pH range.
rows.Finding quote: We found that both APOE3 and APOE4 astrocytes had standard lysosomal-related pH, with a minimal but significant difference of 0.14 pH units between genotypes, APOE4 lysosomes being more alkaline (Fig. 4g).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher acidic-organelle pH)
rows.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; donor age unspecified and sex identity lost; 10% FBS, ratiometric LysoSensor Yellow/Blue DND-160 fluorometry calibrated with monensin and nigericin.

rows.Finding description: APOE4 astrocytes had a larger perinuclear lysosome fraction, reported at 10 μm from the nuclear center as 37% versus 21% in APOE3 cells; N was three, with 30–40 cells quantified.
rows.Finding quote: Specifically, 37% of lysosomes are placed at 10 μm from the center of the nucleus in APOE4 cells, as compared to 21% in APOE3 astrocytes.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (greater perinuclear accumulation of LAMP1-positive compartments)
rows.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; donor age unspecified and sex identity lost; LAMP1 immunofluorescence, confocal microscopy, and Imaris distance analysis of vesicles larger than 0.5 μm relative to the nuclear center.

rows.Finding description: In APOE4 astrocytes, Ned-19 strongly reduced ATP-evoked cytosolic calcium responses, bringing them to a magnitude similar to APOE3 responses.
rows.Finding quote: Interestingly, Ned-19 greatly reduced Ca2+ responses in APOE4 astrocytes, such that purinergic-mediated Ca2+ responses in the presence of Ned-19 were of similar magnitude in both cell types.
rows.Finding summary: (NAADP-pathway inhibition in APOE4 astrocytes) -> (lower acidic-store-dependent ATP-evoked calcium responses)
rows.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE3 or APOE4, provided by Holtzman; donor age unspecified and sex identity lost through aneuploidy; 10% FBS, 100 μM Ned-19 for 20 minutes versus 0.1% DMSO, 100 μM ATP, fura-2/AM imaging.

rows.Finding description: GPN-induced cytosolic calcium AUC was greater in APOE4 than APOE3 astrocytes, supporting greater calcium content in lysosome-enriched acidic stores.
rows.Finding quote: The results showed greater AUC in APOE4 cells (Fig. 4d), supporting a higher concentration of lysosomal-related Ca2+ in APOE4 cells, as compared to APOE3.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (greater GPN-releasable acidic-store calcium)
rows.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; donor age unspecified and sex identity lost; 10% FBS, 200 μM GPN, fura-2/AM cytosolic calcium AUC used to infer acidic-store calcium content.

rows.Finding description: Bafilomycin reduced ATP-evoked calcium responses in APOE4 astrocytes, supporting dependence of their hyperactivity on acidic stores.
rows.Finding quote: Accordingly, bafilomycin A1 reduced the ATP-induced Ca2+ release in APOE4 astrocytes, confirming the dependence of these Ca2+ responses on acidic stores (Fig. 4e).
rows.Finding summary: (V-ATPase inhibition in APOE4 astrocytes) -> (lower ATP-evoked calcium responses)
rows.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE4; donor age unspecified and sex identity lost; 10% FBS, 2 μM bafilomycin A1 for 20 minutes versus DMSO, 100 μM ATP, fura-2/AM imaging.

rows.Finding description: APOE4 astrocytes had higher expression of lysosomal V-ATPase subunit V0D1 than APOE3 astrocytes.
rows.Finding quote: Indeed, the expression of V-ATPase subunit V0D1, which is highly expressed in astrocytes [61], was higher in APOE4 cells than in APOE3 cells (Fig. 4f).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher V-ATPase subunit V0D1 protein expression)
rows.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; donor age unspecified and sex identity lost; V0D1 western blot normalized to β-actin.

rows.Finding description: Bafilomycin increased basal cytosolic calcium in APOE4 astrocytes from 0.30 ± 0.01 to 0.40 ± 0.05 fluorescence-ratio units.
rows.Finding quote: Bafilomycin A1 increased basal cytoplasmic Ca2+ concentration in APOE4 astrocytes to 0.40 ± 0.05 (control values of astrocytes treated with vehicle were 0.30 ± 0.01; p-value = 0.05), whereas there was no effect on non-stimulated intracellular Ca2+ levels in APOE3 (0.44 ± 0.08 for cells treated with bafilomycin A1 compared to 0.39 ± 0.02 of cells treated with vehicle).
rows.Finding summary: (V-ATPase inhibition in APOE4 astrocytes) -> (higher basal cytosolic calcium)
rows.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE4; donor age unspecified and sex identity lost; 10% FBS, 2 μM bafilomycin A1 for 20 minutes versus DMSO, basal fura-2/AM fluorescence ratio.

rows.Finding description: None of the 19 identified lysosomal lipids showed a significant APOE4-versus-APOE3 difference after FDR correction, despite mixed phospholipid changes and increased carnitine.
rows.Finding quote: We could identify 19 lipids: 10 phosphatidylcholines (6 increased, 4 decreased), 5 phosphatidylethanolamine (2 increased, 3 decreased), 2 lysophosphatidylcholine (2 decreased), 1 lysophosphatidylethanolamine (decreased), and 1 carnitine (increased) (Fig. 8d). However, multi t-test analysis corrected by a false discovery rate (FDR) of these 19 FC values gave no statistically significant differences (q-value < 0.05).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no significant change in individual identified lysosomal lipids after FDR correction)
rows.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; donor age unspecified and sex identity lost; isolated lysosomal membrane lipidomics, accurate-mass lipid identification, APOE4/APOE3 fold changes, and multiple t-tests with 5% FDR correction.

rows.Finding description: Removing extracellular lipids produced no significant difference in GPN-estimated acidic-store calcium content in APOE4 astrocytes.
rows.Finding quote: Surprisingly, measurement of Ca2+ stored inside acidic organelles using the GPN-elicited depletion showed no increased Ca2+ loading in APOE3 cells kept in KH (Fig. 7b) compared to APOE3 astrocytes kept in the presence of FBS, whereas, as expected, no difference was observed between the two conditions in APOE4 astrocytes (Fig. 7c).
rows.Finding summary: (FBS-containing medium -> lipid-free KH in APOE4 astrocytes) -> (no change in acidic-store calcium content)
rows.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE4; donor age unspecified and sex identity lost; acute lipid-free Krebs medium versus DMEM with FBS, 200 μM GPN, fura-2/AM cytosolic calcium AUC.

rows.Finding description: Analysis of 35 lysosomal membrane lipids selected by VIP > 1 found significant APOE4-versus-APOE3 differences, with identified lipid species changing in both directions.
rows.Finding quote: In lysosomal membranes, there were 35 lipids with VIP > 1 in the APOE4 vs APOE3. ANOVA analysis with a Tukey correction post-test of the intensity (peak values) of these 35 metabolites revealed significant differences due to the APOE phenotype with a p-value < 0.05, confirming, again, that expression of APOE4 alters the lipidome of lysosomes. We then proceeded to identification of the particular metabolites and calculation of their fold change (FC) in APOE4 vs APOE3 astrocytes. We could identify 19 lipids: 10 phosphatidylcholines (6 increased, 4 decreased), 5 phosphatidylethanolamine (2 increased, 3 decreased), 2 lysophosphatidylcholine (2 decreased), 1 lysophosphatidylethanolamine (decreased), and 1 carnitine (increased) (Fig. 8d).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (mixed changes in selected lysosomal membrane lipids)
rows.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; donor age unspecified and sex identity lost; isolated lysosomal membrane untargeted lipidomics, VIP selection, and ANOVA with Tukey correction.

rows.Finding description: Lysosomal membrane lipid profiles separated APOE4 from APOE3 astrocytes by PLS-DA, providing a compositional surrogate rather than a direct measure of impaired lysosomal function.
rows.Finding quote: The multivariate analysis PLS-DA revealed that the lipids of lysosomal membranes (Fig. 8b) and whole-membranes (Fig. 8c) clustered independently in APOE3 and APOE4 genotypes.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (altered lysosomal membrane lipid composition)
rows.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; donor age unspecified and sex identity lost; lysosomes isolated by density gradients, membranes separated after freeze–thaw disruption, untargeted mass-spectrometry lipidomics and PLS-DA.

rows.Finding description: In the APOE3 control arm, bafilomycin produced no significant difference in ATP-evoked calcium responses.
rows.Finding quote: In contrast, bafilomycin A1 did not change purinergic-induced Ca2+ responses in APOE3 astrocytes.
rows.Finding summary: (V-ATPase inhibition in APOE3 astrocytes) -> (no change in ATP-evoked calcium responses)
rows.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE3, studied alongside APOE4 cells; donor age unspecified; 10% FBS, 2 μM bafilomycin A1 for 20 minutes versus DMSO, 100 μM ATP, fura-2/AM imaging.

rows.Finding description: In the APOE3 control arm, bafilomycin produced no significant difference in basal cytosolic calcium, with values of 0.44 ± 0.08 versus 0.39 ± 0.02.
rows.Finding quote: Bafilomycin A1 increased basal cytoplasmic Ca2+ concentration in APOE4 astrocytes to 0.40 ± 0.05 (control values of astrocytes treated with vehicle were 0.30 ± 0.01; p-value = 0.05), whereas there was no effect on non-stimulated intracellular Ca2+ levels in APOE3 (0.44 ± 0.08 for cells treated with bafilomycin A1 compared to 0.39 ± 0.02 of cells treated with vehicle).
rows.Finding summary: (V-ATPase inhibition in APOE3 astrocytes) -> (no change in basal cytosolic calcium)
rows.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE3, studied alongside APOE4 cells; donor age unspecified; 10% FBS, 2 μM bafilomycin A1 for 20 minutes versus DMSO, basal fura-2/AM fluorescence ratio.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 adheres more tightly to some recycling receptors than APOE3, impeding recycling.

rows.Finding description: Across three independent experiments in primary mouse neurons treated with Reelin, human ApoE4 reduced surface ApoER2 more than ApoE3.
rows.Finding quote: Receptor surface levels show a stronger reduction with ApoE4 than ApoE3.
rows.Finding summary: (ApoE3 -> ApoE4) -> (lower neuronal surface ApoER2 during Reelin stimulation)
rows.Experimental system: Primary cortical neurons isolated from E18 Slc9a6 wildtype mouse embryos, with female Slc9a6+/+ and male Slc9a6y/+ littermates represented; no AD-model mutation reported for this assay. At DIV10–14, neurons received human ApoE3 or ApoE4 conditioned medium from transfected HEK293 cells, 5 μg/ml for 30 minutes, followed by Reelin, 2 μg/ml for another 30 minutes. Surface ApoER2 was measured by sulfo-NHS-SS-biotin labeling, NeutrAvidin isolation, and immunoblotting, with total receptor immunoblots. This measures receptor surface availability as a recycling readout, not apoE binding strength or dissociation kinetics; the brain cells were mouse, not human.

rows.Finding description: Across three independent experiments in primary mouse neurons treated with Reelin, adding human ApoE4 reduced surface ApoER2 compared with the condition without added apoE.
rows.Finding quote: ApoE-conditioned media treatment reduces the surface expression of Apoer2 and glutamate receptors in presence of Reelin in primary neurons. Receptor surface levels show a stronger reduction with ApoE4 than ApoE3.
rows.Finding summary: (No added apoE -> added ApoE4) -> (lower neuronal surface ApoER2 during Reelin stimulation)
rows.Experimental system: Primary cortical neurons from E18 Slc9a6 wildtype mouse embryos, assayed at DIV10–14; no AD-model mutation reported. Human ApoE4 was supplied in HEK293 conditioned medium at 5 μg/ml for 30 minutes before a further 30-minute Reelin treatment at 2 μg/ml; the comparator lacked added apoE. Surface ApoER2 was measured by surface biotinylation, NeutrAvidin isolation, and immunoblotting. The endpoint assesses surface availability associated with recycling, without measuring receptor–apoE binding or dissociation; these were mouse brain cells.

rows.Finding description: Across three independent experiments, germline NHE6 deletion completely restored the ApoER2 recycling readout in primary mouse neurons exposed to human ApoE4 and Reelin. Class 5 (other): Class 5 because the experiment holds APOE4 fixed and manipulates NHE6/endosomal pH, a mediator rather than APOE genotype or isoform, so it tests mediation of the receptor-recycling defect, not A itself.
rows.Finding quote: Apoer2 recycling was completely restored in Slc9a6- neurons treated with ApoE4 (Figure 4C).
rows.Finding summary: (NHE6 present -> NHE6 deleted, with ApoE4) -> (restored neuronal surface ApoER2)
rows.Experimental system: Primary cortical neurons from E18 germline Slc9a6-knockout mouse embryos and wildtype littermates, including female Slc9a6-/- and male Slc9a6y/- knockouts; no AD-model mutation reported. At DIV10–14, cultures received HEK293-secreted human ApoE4 at 5 μg/ml for 30 minutes, followed by Reelin at 2 μg/ml for another 30 minutes. Surface biotinylation and immunoblotting quantified ApoER2 surface availability. Endosomal pH and apoE–receptor binding were not measured in this neuronal panel; the cells were mouse, not human.

rows.Finding description: The APOER2 fraction colocalizing with early endosomes increased from 0.37 in APOE3 to 0.50 in APOE4 neurons, with 20 and 31 cells respectively from three preparations.
rows.Finding quote: Similar analysis of the effect of the APOE genotype on the colocalization of APOER2 with the early endosomes revealed an opposite effect to that seen with LRP1; Accordingly, more APOER2 is localized in the early endosomes in APOE4 cells as indicated by the M1 colocalization variable described in the material and methods section (0.50±0.03, N = 31 from 3 different preparations) than in the APOE3 cells (0.37±0.04, N = 20 from 3 different preparations) neurons (p < 0.05).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher fraction of APOER2 colocalizing with early endosomes)
rows.Experimental system: Brain-derived neuron-enriched primary cultures from 1–3-day-old human-APOE3/4 targeted-replacement mice on an α-synuclein-null background; DIV21; APOER2/Rab5 double staining, confocal microscopy and M1 colocalization.

rows.Finding description: The LRP1 fraction colocalizing with early endosomes decreased from 0.24 in APOE3 to 0.11 in APOE4 neurons, with 21 and 27 cells respectively from two preparations.
rows.Finding quote: Evaluation of the extent of colocalization of the ApoE receptors with the early endosomes (marked in yellow pixels in Fig. 5) revealed that there is a greater localization of LRP1 in early endosomes in APOE3 neurons (0.24±0.02, N = 21 from 2 different preparations) compared to APOE4 (0.11±0.016, N = 27 from 2 different preparations). This difference between the APOE4 and the APOE3 cells is highly significant (p < 0.001).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower fraction of LRP1 colocalizing with early endosomes)
rows.Experimental system: Brain-derived neuron-enriched primary cultures from 1–3-day-old human-APOE3/4 targeted-replacement mice on an α-synuclein-null background; DIV21; LRP1/Rab5 double staining, confocal microscopy and M1 colocalization.

rows.Finding description: LRP1 recycling-endosomal colocalization showed no significant difference between APOE4 and APOE3 neurons, measured in 25–37 cells from two to three preparations.
rows.Finding quote: The first pattern which was observed with LRP1, shows that lower levels of colocalization of this receptor in the early endosomes in APOE4 neurons (seen also in Fig. 5) was accompanied by lower levels of their colocalization with late endosomes (46.7% decrease, p < 0.01) and lysosomes (20.2% decrease, p < 0.05), while no difference between the genotypes was seen in the corresponding recycling endosomes.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in LRP1 colocalization with recycling endosomes)
rows.Experimental system: Brain-derived neuron-enriched primary cultures from 1–3-day-old human-APOE3/4 targeted-replacement mice on an α-synuclein-null background; DIV21; LRP1/Rab11 double staining, confocal microscopy and M1 colocalization.

rows.Finding description: APOER2 knockdown in APOE4 neurons caused no significant difference in LRP1 colocalization with early endosomes. Class 5 (other): Class 5 because APOE4 is held fixed and a receptor (LRP1 or APOER2) is knocked down, which does not act on APOE genotype or isoform.
rows.Finding quote: Additionally, knock-down of APOER2 did not affect the intracellular localization of LRP1.
rows.Finding summary: (APOER2 knockdown in APOE4 neurons) -> (no change in LRP1 colocalization with early endosomes)
rows.Experimental system: Brain-derived primary neurons from neonatal human-APOE4 targeted-replacement mice on an α-synuclein-null background; AAV9 APOER2 gRNA plus Cas9 at DIV3; collection ten days later per CRISPR methods; LRP1/Rab5 confocal M1 analysis in transduced cells.
rows.Data location: Fig. 13B, LRP1, APOE4-APOER2 AAv versus APOE4 control

rows.Finding description: The VEGFR2 fraction colocalizing with early endosomes increased from 0.24 in APOE3 to 0.39 in APOE4 neurons, with 20 and 19 cells respectively from two preparations.
rows.Finding quote: Quantification of these results revealed that the colocalization of IR with early endosomes was significantly higher in APOE4 neurons (0.36±0.02, N = 34 from 4 different preparations) than in the APOE3 neurons (0.28±0.02, N = 48, from 4 different preparations, p < 0.05), as was the colocalization of VEGFR with early endosomes which was higher in APOE4 neurons (0.39±0.03, N = 19 from 2 different preparations) than and in APOE3 neurons (0.24±0.02, N = 20, from 2 different preparations, p < 0.01).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher fraction of VEGFR2 colocalizing with early endosomes)
rows.Experimental system: Brain-derived neuron-enriched primary cultures from 1–3-day-old human-APOE3/4 targeted-replacement mice on an α-synuclein-null background; DIV21; VEGFR2/Rab5 double staining, confocal microscopy and M1 colocalization.

rows.Finding description: VEGFR2 early-endosomal colocalization increased from 0.22 in APOE3 to 0.36 in APOE4 neurons, measured in 25–37 cells from two to three preparations.
rows.Finding quote: A different colocalization pattern was seen in APOER2, IR, and VEGFR, where the accumulation of these receptors in the early endosomes in APOE4 neurons (see also Figs. 5 and 6) is accompanied with lower levels of colocalization in late endosomes relative to those obtained with APOE3 cells.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher fraction of VEGFR2 colocalizing with early endosomes)
rows.Experimental system: Brain-derived neuron-enriched primary cultures from 1–3-day-old human-APOE3/4 targeted-replacement mice on an α-synuclein-null background; DIV21; VEGFR2/Rab5 double staining, confocal microscopy and M1 colocalization.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: Combined lysosomal and proteasomal inhibition produced substantially less protein accumulation in APOE4 than APOE3 neurons, suggesting reduced baseline clearance through the jointly tested pathways.
rows.Finding quote: In contrast, simultaneous inhibition of proteasomal and lysosomal protein clearance synergistically resulted in protein accumulation in APOE3 cells beyond what can be expected of additive clearance inhibition, while protein accumulation was much less evident in APOE4 neurons (Figures 4E, S4A).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (less additional protein accumulation after combined lysosomal/proteasomal blockade; baseline clearance impairment inferred)
rows.Experimental system: Human female-donor isogenic APOE3/APOE3 and APOE4/APOE4 iPSC-derived mixed neuronal cultures at DIV49; donor had AD; 3-hour treatment with 200 nM bafilomycin A1 plus 10 μM MG-132 versus DMSO; housekeeping-normalized mass-spectrometric protein abundance.

rows.Finding description: Proteomic PC2 responses showed accumulation of clearance-sensitive proteins after combined inhibition in APOE3 neurons, with an attenuated response in APOE4 neurons.
rows.Finding quote: Accordingly, while high PC2-scoring proteins reproducibly accumulated in APOE3 neurons upon blocking lysosomal and proteasomal degradation, the same proteins appeared resilient to clearance inhibition in APOE4 neurons (Figures 4G).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (attenuated proteomic response to combined clearance blockade)
rows.Experimental system: Human female-donor isogenic APOE3/APOE3 and APOE4/APOE4 iPSC-derived mixed neurons at DIV49; donor had AD; 3-hour lysosomal/proteasomal inhibitor treatments; batch-corrected mass-spectrometric protein abundance summarized by PCA PC2.

rows.Finding description: Lysosomal inhibition alone affected similar numbers of proteins in APOE3 and APOE4 neurons, a descriptive similarity without a reported statistical test of the genotype difference.
rows.Finding quote: Each treatment individually had a modest impact on the proteome with a similar number of impacted proteins in both the APOE3 and APOE4 neurons (Figure S4A, Table S6).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (similar numbers of proteins responding to lysosomal inhibition)
rows.Experimental system: Human female-donor isogenic APOE3/APOE3 and APOE4/APOE4 iPSC-derived mixed neurons at DIV49; donor had AD; 200 nM bafilomycin A1 for 3 hours versus DMSO; housekeeping-normalized mass-spectrometric protein-abundance responses.

rows.Finding description: PCA of clearance-inhibition proteomics showed a clearance-blockade response in APOE3 neurons that was attenuated in APOE4 neurons, indirectly suggesting baseline clearance impairment.
rows.Finding quote: We performed a principal component analysis (PCA) to visualize differential effects of clearance inhibitors on the neuronal proteome (Figures S4B–C). PC1 explained 68.4% of the observed variance (Figure S4B) and was primarily associated with the APOE genotype, while PC2 (8.4% of variance) was most associated with clearance blockade. Accordingly, while high PC2-scoring proteins reproducibly accumulated in APOE3 neurons upon blocking lysosomal and proteasomal degradation, the same proteins appeared resilient to clearance inhibition in APOE4 neurons (Figures 4G).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (attenuated proteomic response to clearance blockade)
rows.Experimental system: Human female-donor isogenic APOE3/APOE3 and APOE4/APOE4 iPSC-derived mixed neurons at DIV49; donor had AD; 3-hour bafilomycin A1, MG-132, combined treatment, or DMSO; PCA of batch-corrected proteomic intensities.

rows.Finding description: Proteins accumulating after combined clearance blockade in APOE3 neurons were already elevated at APOE4 baseline, including CALM1, CAMKV, APP, and MAPT, indirectly implicating impaired clearance.
rows.Finding quote: By analyzing the clearance-sensitive proteome, we found that several of the proteins accumulating by clearance blockade in APOE3 neurons were elevated at baseline in the APOE4 context (Figure 4H, S4D). This particularly affected synaptic proteins (CALM1, CAMKV), but also extended to the central AD hallmark proteins amyloid precursor protein (APP) and Tau (MAPT; Figure 4H).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher baseline abundance of proteins sensitive to combined clearance blockade)
rows.Experimental system: Human female-donor isogenic APOE3/APOE3 and APOE4/APOE4 iPSC-derived mixed neurons at DIV49; donor had AD; baseline and 3-hour treatment with bafilomycin A1 and/or MG-132; mass-spectrometric protein abundance.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: Compared with ApoE3, ApoE4 increased cholesterol accumulation in lysosomes of PHF-treated BV2 microglia, assessed by filipin and LysoTracker imaging in 8–18 fields from three biological replicates.
rows.Finding quote: ApoE4 significantly increased the accumulation of cholesterol in lysosomes of microglia treated with PHF compared to ApoE3, while treatment with capsaicin significantly decreased it (Fig. 5k, l).
rows.Finding summary: (ApoE3 -> ApoE4, with PHF) -> (increased lysosomal cholesterol accumulation)
rows.Experimental system: Mouse BV2 immortalized microglial cells, not non-aged human brain cells. Recombinant human ApoE3 or ApoE4, 4 μg/ml for 6 h with 10% FBS, washing and 4 h in fresh medium, then 1 μg/ml tau PHF for 24 h. Lysosomes were labeled with 50 nM LysoTracker Red for 30 min and cholesterol with filipin III; confocal imaging assessed lysosomal cholesterol accumulation.

rows.Finding description: In the ApoE isoform treatment experiment, ApoE4 plus PHF produced more autophagosomes relative to autolysosomes, indicating impaired autophagic processing in BV2 microglia; the panel legend reports 10–12 fields from three biological replicates.
rows.Finding quote: We detected increased autophagosomes (remaining yellow dots in Fig. 5i) relative to autolysosomes in microglia treated with ApoE4 in the presence of PHF, indicating impaired autophagy lysosomal pathway.
rows.Finding summary: (ApoE3 -> ApoE4, with PHF) -> (increased autophagosomes relative to autolysosomes)
rows.Experimental system: Mouse BV2 immortalized microglial cell line from the Cell Bank of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, not non-aged human brain cells. Recombinant human ApoE3 or ApoE4, 4 μg/ml for 6 h with 10% FBS, followed by washing, 4 h in fresh medium and 1 μg/ml tau PHF for 24 h. Fixed-cell tandem mRFP-GFP-LC3 fluorescence imaging assessed autophagosome versus autolysosome puncta. No donor age or strain background was reported.

rows.Finding description: Capsaicin restored the tandem LC3 reporter pattern interpreted as autophagic processing in ApoE4-plus-PHF BV2 microglia, with 10–12 fields from three biological replicates; this tests rescue at fixed ApoE4 exposure.
rows.Finding quote: Treatment with TRPV1 agonist capsaicin restored the autophagy lysosomal pathway in microglia (Fig. 5i, j).
rows.Finding summary: (vehicle -> capsaicin, with ApoE4 and PHF) -> (restored autophagy lysosomal pathway)
rows.Experimental system: Mouse BV2 immortalized microglial cells loaded with recombinant human ApoE4, 4 μg/ml for 6 h in 10% FBS, washed and incubated for 4 h in fresh medium. Cells received vehicle or 1 μM capsaicin for 30 min before 1 μg/ml tau PHF for 24 h. Tandem mRFP-GFP-LC3 fluorescence images assessed autophagosome and autolysosome puncta.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 undergoes increased aggregation in the endo-lysosome compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Adding SPA reduced apoE4 aggregation toward the apoE3 level during static light scattering at 37 °C, with three replicates. Class 5 (other): Class 5 because a small molecule (SPA) was added to apoE4 rather than changing the APOE isoform (A), and aggregation was measured cell-free rather than in the endo-lysosome.
rows.Finding quote: The signal from light scattering decreased in the presence of both SPA (Fig. 5A) and tramiprosate (Supplementary Fig. 10), suggesting the reduction of ApoE4 aggregation.
rows.Finding summary: (SPA added to apoE4) -> (reduced apoE aggregation)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human wild-type apoE4 at approximately 10 µM, with 20 mM SPA, a 2000-fold molar excess. Static light scattering at 266 nm over 15 hours in Tris buffer at 37 °C and pH 7.4; apoE3 served as a comparator.

rows.Finding description: In simulations, the dominant W34 side-chain population was around χ1 = 180° in apoE3M and around χ1 = 300° in apoE4M.
rows.Finding quote: We found that ApoE3M displayed a majority of its population around χ1 = 180° while ApoE4M was mostly around χ1 = 300°.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3M -> apoE4M) -> (different W34 conformation at the self-association interface)
rows.Experimental system: Adaptive molecular dynamics of full-length human apoE3M and homology-modeled apoE4M, with five C-terminal monomerizing mutations. Twenty microseconds cumulative sampling per system at 310 K and pH 7.4 protonation; W34 χ1 distributions measured. Structural surrogate, not an aggregate measurement.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: Following Aβ42 treatment, lysosomal inhibition produced greater intracellular Aβ42 accumulation in APOE3 than isogenic APOE4 astrocytes, suggesting reduced lysosome-dependent Aβ42 degradation in APOE4 cells, although lipid mediation was not tested.
rows.Finding quote: Since lysosomal activity can affect Aβ levels, we also examined lysosome-dependent degradation of Aβ42 by measuring intracellular Aβ with or without lysosomal inhibitors following Aβ42 treatment. We observed increased Aβ42 accumulation following lysosome inhibition in APOE3 astrocytes compared to APOE4 astrocytes, suggesting reduced lysosome-dependent Aβ42 degradation in APOE4 astrocytes (Figure S3D).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower inferred lysosome-dependent Aβ42 degradation in human iPSC-derived astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived astrocytes from unaffected female donor line AG09173, donor age 75, comparing parental homozygous APOE3 with CRISPR/Cas9-generated isogenic homozygous APOE4; cultured differentiated cells, with no cellular-aging intervention reported. Intracellular Aβ42 was measured after Aβ42 treatment with or without lysosomal inhibitors. Methods specify 48-hour treatment with leupeptin (50 μM), chloroquine (50 μM), and ammonium chloride (10 mM). The supplementary panel and its complete assay details were unavailable.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: Sixteen hours after apoptotic-neuron injection, confocal imaging showed greater accumulation of LAMP1-positive lysosomes in APOE4-expressing than APOE3-expressing mouse microglia.
rows.Finding quote: Immunostaining of microglia in the injection site showed accumulation of LAMP1+ lysosomes in IBA1+ APOE4-expressing microglia compared to in APOE3-expressing microglia (Fig. 1i,j).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (greater accumulation of LAMP1-positive lysosomes in microglia)
rows.Experimental system: Mouse cortical and hippocampal microglia in 8-month-old human APOE3-knock-in versus APOE4-knock-in mice, without an APP/PS1 or P301S background in this experiment; fluorescent apoptotic primary mouse neurons injected stereotaxically, followed 16 hours later by confocal IBA1/LAMP1 immunostaining; lipid mediation and lysosomal degradation, acidification, and flux were not measured.
